failure_modes: Earth trees seen during the out-of-body phase, not in the other world (two Finland-in-winter passages: 'the trees are supposedly dead, but they were so alive')

Ordinary-life trees seen with new eyes while walking on earth (two near-duplicate passages, IYhYhyenAWE / AMuNQl3Sxa0)
Biography: childhood village with rivers and trees; a Mekong delta treeline from a war memoir

best_quote.text: I look at a trunk on a tree, it looks dirty to me, but these trees were a brilliant, brilliant brown with a tint of gold on

failure_modes: A vision seen during automatic writing rather than during an NDE ('while I was writing, I kept seeing this image in my mind's eye of these rolling hills')
Ordinary biography: driving home 'down this beautiful hilly country highway' before the cardiac event
A portal vision during meditation ('I got so excited... it poofed away... that's what my logo is')

best_quote.text: Over in the far distance, I could see mountains that were 10 times the size of Everest, see buildings that were 10 times the size of what they're now building in Dubai.

failure_modes: Medevac airlift: three passages (two speakers) where 'flying through the clouds' turns out to be a real helicopter ride - the giveaway is the big H on the ground
Idiom and metaphor: 'you're still walking on clouds, aren't you?', 'you're not going to just go up into the clouds and ignore everything'
Explicit cliche-denial rather than perception: 'we aren't just sitting on the clouds eating grapes'
Scripture exposition (Jesus 'taken up into the clouds'), childhood imaginings of heaven, and a past-life regression session

best_quote.text: I started jumping on clouds. I was like, wow, this is so cool. and then jumping from one cloud to another, hugging every cloud

failure_modes: Ordinary homesickness: moving to Ohio, going away to college at 18, a child put on antidepressants who says 'I wasn't homesick. I was confused and broken'
General theorising rather than own report: 'certain types of depression can be related to a type of homesickness for our true home'
Interviewer and audience questions about minimising clients' homesickness; a practitioner describing experiencers in the third person
Inverted direction: homesickness for EARTH felt while out there ('When the Pacific Ocean appeared in its familiar shape, I felt homesick')
Missing loved ones rather than a place

failure_modes: 'Waiting room' as an otherworldly place, not the hospital one: 'heaven's waiting room', a light-filled waiting room, a receiving area for the newly dead, a glass waiting room floating in space
The experiencer or a relative physically sitting in a hospital waiting room in ordinary time - oncology appointments, four hours bleeding before surgery, a deathbed vigil
Second-hand comfort rather than perception: 'Knowing that our friends were in the waiting room and praying for us meant so much to me' (two near-duplicate passages)
A revival scene where the experiencer physically walks to the waiting room after coming round

best_quote.text: I went into the waiting room, where I saw my stepdad get a candy bar. He was like a health nut, so I thought that's odd.

failure_modes: The regex is keying on the bare word 'evil' and catches moral/philosophical use above all: 'even the most evil, death, destruction, disease, is essential', 'at the soul level it does not exist', karma discussions
Biography: an 'evil relationship', 'pure, pure evil witches', an abusive grandfather seen in an ayahuasca ceremony
Sleep paralysis, haunted houses and alien-abduction episodes outside any near-death event - these supply the only formless 'evil presence in the room' language in the packet
Negations, which the regex cannot tell from affirmations: 'No evil was there', 'the next realm where there's no presence of evil of any kind', 'this laughter wasn't like some evil presence'
Where evil IS met during the experience it has a face - a woman who turns, a demon, Satan - which is the node this one is supposed to be distinct from

Ongoing channelled contact with a 'council' outside any NDE: beings arriving while eating Cheerios, automatic-writing sessions (two passages, same speaker), thirteen nights of visits from twelve elders at a ranch (two passages), a spirit team of wisdom keepers
Host intros and channel boilerplate: 'was introduced to the Council of Light where he experienced a life review', 'she met a council of vibrational beings'

Interviewer speculation ('I think that's because a lot of times in near-death experiences people see the council of 12 elders') and third-party accounts (Aaron Green's pre-birth plan, a channeler's 'council of 12 angels')
Bare label with no scene: 'whether you want to call him Council of 11 or whatever you want to'
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:met|stood before|sat before|was (?:brought|taken) before|found myself before)[^.]{0,40}(?:council|elders)|(?:council|elders)[^.]{0,80}(?:semi-?circle|long table|around the table|seated|chuckl\w+))

best_quote.text: I actually was sitting in front of this semi-circle table, and I was in the center, facing the semicircle table. And God was opposite me with elders.

failure_modes: Ordinary-life smells: a dying cat, cigarette smoke on returning to the body, a supermarket smell-association story

Third-party material: hypnotherapy clients reporting sulfur, a shamanic medicine journey, a researcher's Bible/brimstone exposition and a Sodom retelling with no smell at all
A post-NDE phantosmia after-effect from nerve damage ('phantom taste and smell'), not the hell smell clinging
One passage with no smell content whatsoever (matched on 'brimstone' inside a denial)

best_quote.text: there was a stench, an odor of death and decay, a smell that you would associate with a grave

failure_modes: Ordinary-life architecture: 'it was marble walls in this bank'
A crystalline structure used as a diagram of life decisions rather than a building ('heaven looked like a snowflake made out of crystal')

best_quote.text: The other buildings were made out of living stone. It's kind of like white quartz, but you can see the swirling white in the stone.

failure_modes: The sermon form dominates: 'we have forgotten who we are' as general teaching about humanity - at least eight passages, none reporting an event inside an experience
Interviewer questions built on that phrase ('you said that we've forgotten who we are. Do you feel like that is by design?')
Biography: a medium who 'forgot who I was and what my life purpose was' growing up; post-discharge memory confusion explicitly NOT identity loss
Recognition of something else - an angel, a dragon - phrased as 'it was like I had always known this presence'
Ego-dissolution in a dream ('so profound that I forgot who I was') and a translation artefact ('I forgot say that I'm from Gaucha')
audits.suggested_regex: (?:I (?:suddenly |instantly |finally |once again )?(?:remembered|recalled) (?:exactly )?who I (?:really |truly )?(?:was|am)|veil of forgetting (?:was )?(?:lifted|drawn back|pulled back|removed))

best_quote.text: I remembered why I came here. I remembered who I am. I remembered what's happening.

failure_modes: Comparative-religion talk rather than a naming: 'if I was a Buddhist, I would call the light Buddha. If I was a Hindu, it would be Krishna' (two near-duplicate passages), 'one person will say I saw Buddha, the other will say I saw Krishna'
Second-hand reports: 'some saw Buddha, some saw Jesus', a Burmese monk who saw the Buddha in hell (with book plug), a researcher's summary
The historical Buddha as an example in teaching ('Buddha reached the Buddhahood enlightenment'), or as a quoted authority
Names attached to other kinds of experience: a psychedelic session where 'the Happy Buddha appeared in the grass', mystical journeys 'into the mind of Buddha', Brahman/Parabrahman practice phases
Objects and similes: a Buddha statue in an aunt's house, 'it was like I was a little Buddha sitting there on the bed'

best_quote.text: As Christ was gracing me, the light transformed, and within it, I saw the Buddha as a living lotus, the center unfolding endlessly.

failure_modes: Personal opinion rather than taught information, which is the distinction the claim itself rests on: 'I believe that Earth is really a great big classroom', 'I'm a firm believer that we come to this life to learn'
Produced channel narration quoting Vincent Tolman almost verbatim in two separate documents, including a section heading 'Earth School & Your Mission'
Doctrinal 'we believe' framing, scriptural teaching about the first and second death, and new-age ascension teaching ('we are moving to a more advanced school for souls')
Word overlap on 'trip' and 'passing through': a literal trip with a partner, and passing through blue scenery during the NDE journey itself

best_quote.text: he explained that Earth is just a school. That it's always been just a classroom and it's never been a courtroom.

failure_modes: Interviewer-side material: a host reading an audience comment about illusion, a host asking 'would you say this world is not real?', a host aside plus book plug
Literal dreams: a precognitive dream about motorcyclists, a dream of an aunt on a spiral staircase
Generic new-age or mediumistic illusion talk with no anchor to the experience ('because I see beyond the real truth, because this is illusional')
Integration doubt rather than the inversion ('you ask yourself, what is reality? Where is the illusion?')
Adjacent framings that are not the inversion: everything is 'a perception', 'this hologram' used in passing

best_quote.text: It was almost as if my earthly life is the dream state and this heaven that I was standing in was actually my real reality.

failure_modes: Second-hand summary of what NDErs in general see: 'a lot of NDEers will talk about, in their life review, they saw...', 'anybody's had a life review knows', a practitioner describing 'a person' experiencing it

Channel intro boilerplate ('In her life review, Nikesha Burell was shown three specific scenes')
Hypothetical speculation ('if Hitler had a life review... how that's rippled')
Channelled teaching about a future collective 'living life review' for humanity rather than the speaker's own

best_quote.text: I was shown my life in a three-dimensional panoramic view, meaning that I saw everything forward and backward. And every single ripple effect of my every thought, action, out to infinity
